# v1.1.0-dev.58 — Display zoom and resolution mapping, planned

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.57`.

Documentation only. The binary is unchanged from dev.57 — same
features, same behavior, same settings. Auto-update will pick
this up because the tag is newer, and you lose nothing by
skipping it.

What lands here is the design work for a feature that's been
asked for: a global hotkey that changes the Windows display
scaling percentage, and a way to tie a zoom level to specific
resolutions.

## Why This Needed A Plan First

Half of the feature has no documented API.

Resolution is easy. `EnumDisplaySettingsExW` and
`ChangeDisplaySettingsExW` have been stable since Windows 95,
and `DEVMODEW` is a published struct.

The scaling percentage is not. Windows exposes no supported way
to set it. The Settings app does it through
`DisplayConfigSetDeviceInfo` with two undocumented
`DISPLAYCONFIG_DEVICE_INFO_TYPE` values that were recovered by
reading `user32.dll`. Microsoft can change or remove those in
any build with no notice, so the plan puts them behind a
capability probe that reports a specific reason when the call
isn't available. The documented half can never be taken down by
the undocumented half, and a failure says what went wrong
instead of quietly doing nothing.

## What The Design Settles

**Display config becomes a property of a profile.** A profile
picks up an optional `displayMode` block, and a profile that
carries one with no windows in it is a zoom preset. That means a
zoom preset gets a hotkey through the capture modal you already
use, shows up in the tray menu, the Jump List, the command
palette, `--load=`, and `wlm://` — with no new code in any of
them. A separate preset type would have needed all of that
taught about a second kind of hotkey owner.

**Scale ships before resolution.** The split falls on something
measurable rather than on taste. A scale change leaves monitor
bounds untouched, so a monitor-set-bound profile keeps matching.
A resolution change moves bounds, and a large one drops the
match below the threshold and breaks the binding. Shipping scale
first gets the hotkey working without putting existing bindings
at risk.

**Auto-activation has to be taught to ignore WLM's own display
changes.** Right now a `WM_DISPLAYCHANGE` is treated as your
intent, which is correct — until WLM is the thing causing it. Left
alone, a zoom hotkey could relocate every window, pop the
profile chooser, or fire a profile's post-load hook. The plan
fingerprints the monitor layout while deliberately ignoring DPI,
so a scale change is invisible to the fingerprint and can be
told apart from a real monitor being plugged in.

**Parsec virtual displays get called out specifically.** There's
an open Windows 11 24H2 bug where `ChangeDisplaySettingsEx`
stops taking effect on virtual displays from user mode while
still reporting success. That lands on exactly the hardware this
app exists for, so the resolution half is gated behind measuring
it on a real machine first rather than assuming it works.

## Where To Find It

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-14-display-zoom-resolution-design.md`
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-14-display-zoom-resolution.md`

Both documents carry a banner explaining that their `file:line`
anchors were taken against an older checkout and need
re-verifying before anyone works from them. The design holds —
no display or scaling code exists yet — but the line numbers
moved.

## What's The Same

no behavior change.
